newsitem.title: UK: Fidelity still to hear fate from British regulator.
newsitem.headline: Fidelity still to hear fate from British regulator.

text.p: Fidelity Brokerage Services declined to comment on Wednesday on whether it had been informed of any disciplinary action against it or whether restrictions had been lifted by a British financial watchdog.

A spokesman for the group, the British retail stockbroking arm of U.S. fund management giant Fidelity Investments, said he could not comment on the timing or likely outcome of any Securities and Futures Authority (SFA) decision.
In January the SFA extended restrictions until the end of this month on Fidelity Brokerage preventing it from taking on new direct customers or introducing new business services.
The SFA also said it would begin disciplinary action against the firm over problems with its customer service performance.
Last November Fidelity promised to restore "satisfactory" service to clients by January after computer problems stopped it taking on new customers.
It said system problems had resulted in accounting and reconciliation difficulties and promised compensation to any customers who lost out.
The SFA said it would take into account the speed with which Fidelity brought the matters to a satisfactory conclusion in determining the extent of disciplinary proceedings and the penalty imposed.
SFA officials were not immediately available for comment on when they would rule whether the restrictions had been lifted and what disciplinary action would be taken.
